column1: # A CONTAINER'S OWN CONFLICT IS SITED AT THE CONTAINER (BUGS.md 47).
# Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect (errc), and the five-column
# name<TAB>vet<TAB>schema<TAB>data<TAB>expect for the vet rows below.
# When a list or a map meets a peer that is not a list or a map, the
# refusal belongs to the CONTAINER -- no member is party to it. Both
# ports refused correctly and both emitted the same code, but Go named
# a member: ListVal.Unify and MapVal.Unify drive their element and key
# loops through `ctx.slot`, and only the in-branch paths restored it,
# so a stale child slot survived into the not-a-container branch and
# makeNilErr's slot-extension stamped it. `a:[x:1,10,"bad"] &
# {a:[integer,integer,integer]}` reported `$.a.1`, an element that is
# not party to the failure, where TypeScript reported `$.a`.
# The MAP twin was never reported -- it was found by looking for it
# after the list case, and had the identical shape and the identical
# one-line cause.
# The code rows come first and the PATH rows after, because the code was
# never the thing in dispute: both ports agreed on it throughout, so
# every code-only row passed in both engines while the paths disagreed.
# The path is the field `vet --format json` hands an agent, and it
# decides which line a caller is sent to. The four `errc` rows below are
# therefore controls -- they pass with the fix reverted -- and the three
# `vet` rows are the pins.
# Every expectation was obtained by running BOTH engines and diffing,
# per the parity probe.
container-path-list-conjunct-code
container-path-list-scalar-conjunct-code
container-path-map-statements-code
container-path-nested-code
# THE PATH ITSELF IS PINNED THROUGH `vet`, NOT THROUGH `err`. An `err`
# row matches its expectation as a SUBSTRING, and a container's path is
# a PREFIX of every member path below it -- `at path $.a` is contained
# in `at path $.a.2`, so an err row asserting the container would have
# passed against the very answer it was written to forbid. (The whole
# rest of the message is byte-identical between the two, so no other
# substring discriminates either.) A `vet` row compares the finding
# object field by field, where `path` is matched exactly. These three
# fail against the pre-fix engine: `$.a.2`, `$.a.r`, `$.a.b.2`.
container-path-vet-list
container-path-vet-map
container-path-vet-nested
